01 — THE PLUGIN

One toolkit.
Many ways to explore.

Pondskater brings together Grasshopper components for polygons, straight skeletons, roofs, networks and paths. It also includes tools for subdivision, arches and extrusion profiles for 3D concrete printing.

Skeleton, offset and roof operations use Surfer2, developed by the Computational Geometry and Applications Lab at the University of Salzburg, and built on CGAL.

Small steps.

Four setup guides based on the component inputs.
Validate the results in your Grasshopper installation.

01 / BOUNDARIES

Offset a rectangle

Rectangle → Offset → Curves
  1. Create a 20 × 12 rectangle on the XY plane and connect it to Polyline (P) on Offset.
  2. Connect World XY to Plane (Pl). Use Type = True and Direction = 0 for inward offsets.
  3. Connect a Panel containing 3 * 1 to Distances (Di). Leave Weights unconnected to use unit weights.
  4. Inspect Offsets (O) and Skeleton (Sk). This expression repeats three increments of one unit.
View Offset ↗
02 / ANALYSIS

Measure a bounding rectangle

Polyline → MBR → Area
  1. Create a closed polyline on the XY plane without self-intersections.
  2. Connect it to Polyline (P) on Minimum Bounding Rectangle.
  3. Keep Plane = World XY. Connect the outputs Area, Length and Width to Panels.
  4. Display Rectangle (R) over the polygon and rotate the boundary to explore the orientation of the bounding rectangle.
View MBR ↗
03 / PATHS

Traverse a network

Lines + Point → E_Path → Path
  1. Draw three segments connected in a chain: A–B, B–C and C–D.
  2. Connect the list to Curves (C) on Eulerian Path and point A to Start (S).
  3. Keep the document tolerance to merge coincident endpoints.
  4. Check Exists (E). For this chain, the expected path traverses all three edges from A to D.
View Eulerian Path ↗
04 / CONSTRUCTION

Draw an arch

Span + Rise → 3SegArch → Arch
  1. Add Three-Segment Arch to the document.
  2. Connect a slider set to 10 to Span (S) and another set to 3 to Rise (R).
  3. Keep Plane = World XY: the span follows X and the rise follows Y.
  4. Inspect Arch (A), the three segments in AS and their centres in C.
View Three-Segment Arch ↗

BEFORE YOU START

Planes, weights and dependencies.

Use planar geometry and its matching reference plane. In multiplicative mode, each edge speed is w; in additive mode, it is 1 + wa. The two modes cannot be combined in the same input.

Skeleton2d, Offset and Roofer require the native Surfer library. The project uses libsurfer.dylib on macOS and surfer.dll, with dependencies, on Windows. This page documents the local source; it does not provide an installer.
